proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an arbitrary finite scenario list
\(\mathcal H_0=\{h^1,\ldots,h^M\}\subset[-H,H]^K\).  Only finiteness and
\(|h_j^m|\leq H\) are used below.

\emph{Exact embedding.}
Fix \(n\) and \(\pi_n\in\Pi_n\).  On
\(((i-1)/n,i/n]\), define the vertex control
\[
 u_j(t)=\mathbf 1\{A_i=j\}.
\tag{1}
\]
The randomization producing \(A_i\) is made at the left endpoint from
\(\mathcal F_{i-1}\).  Thus (1) is predictable by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\mbox{-}predictability}\), and it belongs to
\(\mathcal U\) by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}continuous\mbox{-}observed\mbox{-}control}\) and
\(\mathrm{def{:}continuous\mbox{-}control\mbox{-}class}\).  Conditional on
the past and \(A_i=j\), the diffusion increments are
\[
 \Delta X_j=\frac{h_j^m}{n}
 +W_j(i/n)-W_j((i-1)/n)
 \sim\mathcal N\!\left(\frac{h_j^m}{n},\frac1n\right),
 \qquad \Delta Q_j=\frac1n,
\tag{2}
\]
and all other coordinates have zero increments.  By
\(\mathrm{ass{:}gaussian\mbox{-}known\mbox{-}variance}\) and
\(\mathrm{ass{:}local\mbox{-}scenario\mbox{-}scaling}\),
\(Y_i/\sqrt n\), conditionally on the same history and action, has exactly
the score law in (2).  Induction over \(i\) proves equality of the complete
observed score--clock laws under every scenario \(m\).  Consequently every
finite policy is embedded exactly as a vertex-control diffusion policy, with
the same scenario-risk vector.

\emph{Continuous-payoff approximation.}
Let \(g_m:\mathbb R^K\times[0,1]^K\to[0,1]\) be continuous for
\(m=1,\ldots,M\).  We first prove convergence of its prior-weighted value
over \(n\)-grid vertex controls to its value over \(\mathcal U\).
On the canonical observed space, a progressively measurable
\(\Delta(\mathcal J)\)-valued control \(u\) can be approximated by simple
predictable controls \(u^{(r)}\): approximate its bounded predictable
coordinates by simple predictable functions and project their vectors onto
the closed simplex.  Bounded convergence in measure gives
\[
 \mathbb E_0\int_0^1\sum_j
 |u_j^{(r)}(t)-u_j(t)|\,dt\longrightarrow0.
\tag{3}
\]
The inequality \((\sqrt a-\sqrt b)^2\leq |a-b|\), for \(a,b\geq0\),
and the Itô isometry show from (3) that the martingale parts of the score
vectors converge in \(L^2(\mathbb P_0)\); the clock vectors converge in
\(L^1(\mathbb P_0)\).  Since \(|h_j^m|\leq H\), the drift terms converge
in \(L^1\) under every scenario as well.

For a fixed simple control, subdivide each of its finitely many time cells
into \(n\)-grid cells.  At the left endpoint of a grid cell, choose vertex
\(j\) with the simplex probabilities prescribed by the simple control.
Within each time cell, the sum of the conditional variances of the
normalized centered allocation counts is at most the reciprocal of the
number of grid cells and hence tends to zero.  Conditional on those counts,
the coordinate score increment has mean \(h_j^m\Delta Q_j\), variance
\(\Delta Q_j\), and characteristic function
\[
 \exp\!\left\{\mathrm i z_jh_j^m\Delta Q_j
 -\frac12z_j^2\Delta Q_j\right\}.
\tag{4}
\]
At the finitely many decision times, each past-measurable action kernel can
be replaced by one continuous outside a set of arbitrarily small
\(\mathbb P_0\)-probability: approximate its bounded coordinate functions
by continuous functions off a small Borel set and project back onto the
simplex.  A union bound over the finitely many cells controls the probability
that any action changes.  Induction over the cells can then apply (4) at
continuity points.  Letting the exceptional probability vanish and then
using (3) yields a diagonal sequence of predictable grid policies
\(\pi_n[u]\) such that
\[
 (X_n,Q_n)\Longrightarrow(X^u(1),Q^u(1))
 \quad\text{under the zero-drift reference law}.
\tag{5}
\]
Vertex randomization allows a simplex coordinate to equal zero, so no
positive allocation lower bound has been added.

We transfer (5) to every declared scenario without treating the adaptive
clock as independent of the score.  Under the zero-drift reference law put
\[
 M_m(t)=\sum_jh_j^m\int_0^t\sqrt{u_j(s)}\,dW_j(s),
 \qquad
 A_m(t)=\langle M_m\rangle_t
 =\sum_j(h_j^m)^2Q_j(t).
\tag{6}
\]
Because \(\sum_jQ_j(1)=1\) and \(|h_j^m|\leq H\),
\[
 0\leq A_m(1)\leq H^2.
\tag{7}
\]
The likelihood ratio from the zero-drift law to scenario \(m\) is
\[
 Z_m(X(1),Q(1))
 =\exp\{M_m(1)-\tfrac12A_m(1)\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Its square factors pathwise as
\[
 Z_m(X(1),Q(1))^2
 =\underbrace{\exp\{2M_m(1)-2A_m(1)\}}_
 {\mathcal E(2M_m)_1}\exp\{A_m(1)\}.
\tag{9}
\]
This is a factorization, not an independence assertion.  Moreover,
\[
 \frac12\langle2M_m\rangle_1=2A_m(1)\leq2H^2.
\tag{10}
\]
For a simple predictable integrand, successive conditional Gaussian
expectations show that \(\mathbb E_0\mathcal E(2M_m)_1=1\).  For a general
progressively measurable control, approximate the bounded integrand in
\(L^2(dt\,d\mathbb P_0)\) by simple predictable integrands.  The stochastic
integrals and brackets then converge in probability.  If \(R\) is any such
simple approximating martingale with energy at most \(4H^2\), the same
factorization and the conditional Gaussian identity at doubled integrand
give
\[
 \mathbb E_0[\mathcal E(R)_1^2]
 =\mathbb E_0[\mathcal E(2R)_1e^{\langle R\rangle_1}]
 \leq e^{4H^2}.
\]
The exponentials are therefore uniformly integrable, and passage to the
limit preserves their mean one.  Combining this bounded-energy conclusion
with (7)--(9) gives the corrected adaptive-clock estimate
\[
 \mathbb E_0[Z_m(X(1),Q(1))^2]
 \leq e^{H^2}\mathbb E_0\mathcal E(2M_m)_1
 =e^{H^2}.
\tag{11}
\]
The same calculation holds for grid vertex controls, whose bracket is
\(\sum_j(h_j^m)^2Q_{j,n}\leq H^2\).  Hence the likelihood ratios of the
approximating controls are uniformly integrable.  Since
\[
 Z_m(x,q)=
 \exp\!\left\{\sum_jh_j^mx_j-\frac12
 \sum_j(h_j^m)^2q_j\right\}
\tag{12}
\]
is continuous, truncation of \(Z_m\), (5), and (11) imply
\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb E_m^{\pi_n[u]}g_m(X_n,Q_n)
 &=\mathbb E_0^{\pi_n[u]}[Z_m(X_n,Q_n)g_m(X_n,Q_n)]\\
 &\longrightarrow
 \mathbb E_0^u[Z_m(X(1),Q(1))g_m(X(1),Q(1))]\\
 &=\mathbb E_m^ug_m(X(1),Q(1)).
 \end{split}
\tag{13}
\]
Because \(M\) is finite, this convergence is simultaneous over all
scenarios.

Let \(G_n(\lambda)\) and \(G(\lambda)\) be the infimal prior-weighted risks
for the continuous payoffs \(g_m\), over \(\Pi_n\) and \(\mathcal U\),
respectively.  Exact embedding gives \(G(\lambda)\leq G_n(\lambda)\).
Conversely, choose a control within an arbitrary positive tolerance of
\(G(\lambda)\) and apply (13).  Therefore
\[
 G_n(\lambda)\longrightarrow G(\lambda).
\tag{14}
\]
For fixed \(\delta>0\), the envelope losses in
\(\mathrm{def{:}terminal\mbox{-}envelopes}\) are bounded and continuous:
exponentiation, finite arithmetic means, finite minima, and
\(f_\delta^\pm\) are continuous.  Thus (14) gives
\[
 B_{n,\delta}^{\pm}(\lambda)
 \longrightarrow B_\delta^{\pm}(\lambda).
\tag{15}
\]
For either sign and either experiment, the value is \(1\)-Lipschitz in
\(\lambda\) under the \(\ell_1\) norm because each scenario loss lies in
\([0,1]\).  A finite \(\ell_1\)-net of the compact simplex \(\Delta_M\),
followed by the two Lipschitz inequalities, upgrades (15) to
\[
 \sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}
 |B_{n,\delta}^{\pm}(\lambda)-B_\delta^{\pm}(\lambda)|
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]

\emph{Removal of the envelopes.}
The scalar inequalities
\(f_\delta^-\leq\mathbf1\{\,\cdot<0\,\}\leq f_\delta^+\) and
\(\mathrm{lem{:}quantitative\mbox{-}terminal\mbox{-}comparison}\) give
\[
 B_{n,\delta}^-(\lambda)\leq B_n(\lambda)\leq
 B_{n,\delta}^+(\lambda),\qquad
 B_\delta^-(\lambda)\leq B(\lambda)\leq
 B_\delta^+(\lambda),
\tag{17}
\]
and each upper-minus-lower width is at most
\(\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\eta)\), uniformly in \(n\) and \(\lambda\).
Combining (16)--(17), with \(\eta=\sqrt\delta\), yields
\[
 \limsup_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}
 |B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|
 \leq \rho_{H,K}(\delta,\sqrt\delta).
\tag{18}
\]
The final assertion of
\(\mathrm{lem{:}quantitative\mbox{-}terminal\mbox{-}comparison}\) permits
\(\delta\downarrow0\), proving
\[
 \sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{19}
\]
At the point-mass prior \(e_m\), the definitions give
\(B_n(e_m)=c_{n,m}\) and \(B(e_m)=c_m\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{1\leq m\leq M}|c_{n,m}-c_m|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{20}
\]

We next transfer the minimax regret.  Let \(C_n\) be the closure in
\([0,1]^M\) of the achievable finite-experiment regret vectors.
Exogenous randomization at time zero makes \(C_n\) convex, and it is compact.
If \(v_n=\min_{r\in C_n}\max_mr_m\), then
\(D_n=C_n+\mathbb R_+^M\) contains \(v_n\mathbf1\), whereas
\((v_n-a)\mathbf1\notin D_n\) for \(a>0\).  For
\(y_k=(v_n-k^{-1})\mathbf1\), let \(d_k\) minimize
\(\|y_k-d\|_2\) over \(d\in D_n\).  Convexity and minimality give
\[
 (d_k-y_k)^\top(d-d_k)\geq0\qquad(d\in D_n).
\]
Set \(\lambda_k=(d_k-y_k)/\|d_k-y_k\|_1\).  Since
\(D_n+\mathbb R_+^M=D_n\), substitution of \(d=d_k+ae_j\) shows that
\((\lambda_k)_j\geq0\), so \(\lambda_k\in\Delta_M\).
Furthermore, \(d_k\to v_n\mathbf1\), because
\(\|d_k-y_k\|_2\leq\sqrt M/k\).  Along a convergent subsequence
\(\lambda_k\to\lambda_n\in\Delta_M\), and passage to the limit gives
\(\lambda_n^\top(d-v_n\mathbf1)\geq0\) for every \(d\in D_n\).
Together with \(\lambda^\top r\leq\max_mr_m\), this proves
\[
 \inf_{r\in C_n}\max_mr_m
 =\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\inf_{r\in C_n}\lambda^\top r.
\tag{21}
\]
Translation by the oracle vector yields
\[
 V_n=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}
 \left\{B_n(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{n,m}\right\}.
\tag{22}
\]
The identical finite-dimensional argument for diffusion risks gives
\[
 V=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}
 \left\{B(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_m\right\}.
\tag{23}
\]
Equations (19)--(23) imply
\[
 |V_n-V|
 \leq\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|
 +\max_m|c_{n,m}-c_m|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{24}
\]

\emph{Predictable policy attainment.}
Fix \(\epsilon>0\).  By (20) and (24), choose \(N\) such that
\[
 |V_N-V|+\max_m|c_{N,m}-c_m|<\epsilon/3.
\tag{25}
\]
Choose \(\pi_N\in\Pi_N\) with
\[
 \max_m\{L_N(\pi_N,m)-c_{N,m}\}\leq V_N+\epsilon/3.
\tag{26}
\]
Embed \(\pi_N\) as the \(N\)-block vertex control \(u^\epsilon\) from
(1).  Equality of its scenario-risk vector and (25)--(26) give
\[
 \max_m r_m(u^\epsilon)\leq V+\epsilon.
\tag{27}
\]

It remains to approximate this control for the original discontinuous
loss.  Conditional on the exogenous randomization and on any action
sequence of positive conditional probability, the sampled Gaussian block
increments are absolutely continuous on their sampled coordinate
subspace.  A terminal threshold equality is a zero set of
\[
 \sum_{j\in I}\exp(X_j-Q_j/2)-20|I|.
\tag{28}
\]
If at least one coordinate \(j_0\in I\) was sampled, condition on all
sampled Gaussian coordinates except \(X_{j_0}\).  Equation (28) has at
most one solution for \(X_{j_0}\), while its conditional law has a density,
so equality has conditional probability zero.  If no coordinate in \(I\)
was sampled, the left side is \(|I|-20|I|\neq0\).  Fubini's identity and
the finiteness of \(\mathcal I\) therefore give
\[
 \Pr_m^{u^\epsilon}\{a_j(X(1),Q(1))=0
 \text{ for some }j\}=0
\quad(1\leq m\leq M).
\tag{29}
\]

For horizon \(n\), divide enrollment into \(N\) consecutive blocks whose
lengths differ from \(n/N\) by at most one, keep the subgroup selected by
\(\pi_N\) throughout each block, and supply its normalized Gaussian block
aggregate to the next decision kernel.  This rule is predictable by
\(\mathrm{ass{:}finite\mbox{-}predictability}\).  The block clock lengths
converge to \(1/N\), and the aggregates have their exact Gaussian laws;
induction over the fixed number \(N\) of blocks gives terminal-state
convergence to \(u^\epsilon\).  Decision kernels may first be modified on
sets of arbitrarily small probability, simultaneously under the finite
family of Gaussian history laws, so that the induction occurs at continuity
points.  By (29), neighborhoods of the finitely many threshold surfaces can
be chosen with arbitrarily small probability.  Off those neighborhoods the
terminal loss is continuous and bounded by one.  Weak convergence there,
followed by shrinking the neighborhoods, gives predictable policies
\(\pi_n^\epsilon\) satisfying
\[
 L_n(\pi_n^\epsilon,m)\longrightarrow L(u^\epsilon,m)
 \quad\text{for every }m.
\tag{30}
\]
Equations (27) and (30) prove the asserted coordinatewise risk-vector
transfer.  The construction permits zero block allocations.  Every step
used only the finite list and \(|h_j^m|\leq H\); null-boundary closure was
not used.

Write \(\ell_{m,\delta}^-\) and \(\ell_{m,\delta}^+\) for the losses in
\(\mathrm{def{:}terminal\mbox{-}envelopes}\).  For every
\(a\in\mathbb R\),
\[
f_\delta^-(a)\leq\mathbf1\{a<0\}\leq f_\delta^+(a).
\tag{31}
\]
Multiplication by the nonnegative weights
\(w_j\mathbf1\{h_j^m>0\}\), followed by summation, gives
\[
0\leq\ell_{m,\delta}^-\leq\ell_m\leq
\ell_{m,\delta}^+\leq1.
\tag{32}
\]
If \(c_{m,\delta}^\pm\) denotes the corresponding oracle value, taking
infima in (32) yields
\[
B_\delta^-(\lambda)\leq B(\lambda)\leq B_\delta^+(\lambda),
\qquad
c_{m,\delta}^-\leq c_m\leq c_{m,\delta}^+.
\tag{33}
\]
These are bounds on observed-law design functionals and do not redefine
the causal regret target \(V\).

\emph{The two continuity moduli.}
Put \(c_H=H+H^2/2\), \(s_k=x_k-q_k/2\), and
\(e_I=|I|^{-1}\sum_{k\in I}\exp(s_k)\).  Along a line segment in
\((x,q)\), either envelope composed with
\(a_j=\min_{I\ni j}e_I-20\) is absolutely continuous.  Wherever its
derivative is nonzero, an active intersection obeys
\[
19<20-\delta\leq e_I\leq20+\delta<21.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sum_{k\in I}\left|\frac{\partial e_I}{\partial x_k}\right|<21,
\qquad
\sum_{k\in I}\left|\frac{\partial e_I}{\partial q_k}\right|<\frac{21}{2}.
\]
Since the envelope slope is at most \(1/\delta\), integration along the
segment gives the conservative bound
\[
|\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm(x,q)-\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm(x',q')|
\leq\frac{32}{\delta}\|(x,q)-(x',q')\|_\infty.
\tag{34}
\]
No division by an allocation clock is used.

For the likelihoods in the frozen core,
\[
d\log Z_m=\sum_jh_j^m\,dx_j-\frac12\sum_j(h_j^m)^2\,dq_j,
\]
and hence, when the state displacement has sup norm at most \(d\),
\[
|\log Z_m-\log Z_m'|\leq Kc_Hd.
\tag{35}
\]
Differentiating the posterior weights gives
\[
db_m^\lambda=b_m^\lambda\left(d\log Z_m-
\sum_rb_r^\lambda d\log Z_r\right),
\]
so
\[
\sum_m|db_m^\lambda|\leq2Kc_Hd.
\tag{36}
\]
This remains valid when prior coordinates vanish.  Thus the normalized
posterior terminal payoff
\(g=\sum_mb_m^\lambda\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm\) has modulus
\[
\Omega_\delta(d)=
\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+2Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\tag{37}
\]

Now fix a guard box and let
\[
C_G=\max_{\text{guard box}}\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m,\qquad
S=\frac{\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m}{C_G}.
\]
Along every segment contained in the guard box, \(0\leq S\leq1\).
Moreover, the logarithmic derivative of \(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\) is the
posterior-weighted average of the logarithmic derivatives of the \(Z_m\)'s.
Equation (35) therefore gives
\[
|S-S'|\leq Kc_Hd.
\tag{38}
\]
Since \(0\leq g,g',S,S'\leq1\),
\[
|Sg-S'g'|\leq |g-g'|+|S-S'|.
\]
Combining this inequality with (37)--(38) proves that the scaled
unnormalized reference datum \(Sg\) has the corrected modulus
\[
\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=
\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+3Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\tag{39}
\]
The outer minimum is essential: once the linear expression reaches one,
the range bound \(0\leq Sg\leq1\) is used.

The relevant modulus propagates backward.  Couple two processes started
from states at the same time by using the same future noise and feeding the
second policy the first history translated by the initial state difference.
Their controls coincide and their terminal score--clock difference equals
the initial difference.  Equations (34)--(39), followed by taking infima in
both directions, give \(\Omega_\delta\) for the normalized posterior value
and \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\) for every scaled unnormalized continuation
value.  The scaled reference-law computation below therefore uses
\(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\) in every interpolation, control-continuity,
mollification, Bellman-residual, finite-horizon accumulation, fixed-policy,
and point-mass-oracle bound.  The coupling remains valid on zero-allocation
faces.

\emph{Validated finite recursion.}
Under the zero-drift reference law, bounded predictability makes
\[
Z_m(X(t),Q(t))=
\exp\!\left\{\sum_jh_j^mX_j(t)
-\frac12\sum_j(h_j^m)^2Q_j(t)\right\}
\tag{40}
\]
a mean-one likelihood process.  Successive Gaussian conditioning proves
this for simple predictable controls.  Approximation in stochastic-integral
norm proves it for general controls because the integrands have energy
bounded by \(H^2\).  Thus, for bounded terminal \(R\),
\[
\mathbb E_m^u[R]=\mathbb E_0^u[Z_m(X(1),Q(1))R].
\tag{41}
\]
The reference terminal datum is consequently
\(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm=C_GSg\).
After division by \(C_G\), its range is \([0,1]\).  At first guard exit the
scaled conditional continuation therefore lies in \([0,1]\); the algorithm
uses this exterior interval and makes no clamping assertion.

Suppose the vertices \(v\) of a viable state cell carry intervals enclosing
a scaled continuation function \(F\), and \(y\) has multilinear barycentric
weights \(\beta_v\).  If the cell diameter is \(d\), (39) gives
\[
\left|F(y)-\sum_v\beta_vF(v)\right|
\leq\sum_v\beta_v\widetilde\Omega_\delta(\|y-v\|_\infty)
\leq\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d).
\tag{42}
\]
Thus the barycentric interval enlarged by the corrected modulus encloses
\(F(y)\).

For a time increment \(a>0\), constant allocation
\(v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\), and standard Gaussian \(z\), the reference
transition is
\[
(x,q)\longmapsto
\bigl(x+(av)^{1/2}\mathbin\odot z,\ q+av\bigr).
\tag{43}
\]
For each retained Gaussian cell, interval arithmetic encloses the entire
image of (43).  Multiplying its nonnegative continuation interval by an
outward-rounded probability interval and summing outward preserves
enclosure; omitted mass is multiplied by \([0,1]\).  Coupling allocations
\(v,v'\) with the same \(z\), using
\((\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\leq|p-q|\), bounds the scaled control-net error by
\[
\mathbb E\,\widetilde\Omega_\delta\!\left(
a\|v-v'\|_1+\sqrt{a\|v-v'\|_1}\,\|z\|_2\right).
\tag{44}
\]
Bounded convergence makes (44) tend uniformly to zero with the control-net
radius.  Taking the minimum of lower endpoints minus this error and of
upper endpoints plus this error encloses the Bellman infimum over the whole
simplex.  Backward induction using (42)--(44) proves enclosure at every
time level.  The identical argument, with the same corrected modulus,
validates fixed-policy and point-mass-oracle recursions.  Gaussian cell
probabilities have effective rational outward bounds obtained from rational
Taylor bounds for \(\exp(-z^2/2)\) on bounded cells; omitted Gaussian mass
is assigned adversarially in \([0,1]\).

\emph{Passage to continuous time.}
Let \(P_a^v\) denote the Gaussian operator in (43), and put
\[
\mathcal L^v\phi=\frac12\sum_jv_j\partial_{x_jx_j}\phi+
\sum_jv_j\partial_{q_j}\phi.
\tag{45}
\]
For the exact regularized recursion on a partition
\(0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=1\), with \(a_l=t_{l+1}-t_l\),
\[
J_l=\min_{v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)}P_{a_l}^vJ_{l+1},
\qquad
J_l\leq P_{a_l}^vJ_{l+1}\quad\text{for every }v.
\tag{46}
\]
Convolve the scaled multilinear lower interpolants on the inner score box
with a rational compactly supported \(C^3\) tensor mollifier of radius
\(\kappa\), whose support lies in the guard box.  Its terminal and
intermediate mollification errors are bounded by
\(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(\kappa)\), not by (37).  Convolution commutes
with \(P_a^v\).  If the one-layer interval error, recomputed using
(39), is \(\xi_l\), subtracting \(\sum_{s\geq l}\xi_s\) restores the
second inequality in (46) for the smoothed lower interpolants.
Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives
\[
P_a^v\phi-\phi-a\mathcal L^v\phi=\mathcal R_a^v(\phi).
\tag{47}
\]
Derivative intervals of the mollified interpolant and truncated Gaussian
moments give outward rational bounds for \(\mathcal R_a^v\).  For fixed
\(\kappa\), the score remainder is bounded by a computable multiple of
\(a^{3/2}\kappa^{-3}\), the clock remainder by a computable multiple of
\(a^2\kappa^{-2}\), and the interpolation contribution by the corrected
\(\xi_l\).  The checked rational refinements include
\[
\max_la_l\downarrow0,\quad
\sum_l\xi_l\downarrow0,\quad
\max_l\frac{\xi_l}{a_l}\downarrow0,\quad
\kappa\downarrow0,\quad
\max_la_l^{1/2}\kappa^{-3}\downarrow0.
\tag{48}
\]
Because \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)\to0\) as \(d\downarrow0\) for fixed
\(\delta\), such refinements exist.

Linear interpolation in time then gives computable errors
\(e_T\geq0\) and \(e_B(t)\geq0\) such that
\[
\phi^-(1,\cdot)\leq
C_G^{-1}\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm,\quad
\phi^-\leq0\ \text{on the guard boundary},\quad
\partial_t\phi^-+\mathcal L^v\phi^-\geq-e_B(t)
\tag{49}
\]
for every \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\), and
\[
e_T+\int_0^1e_B(t)\,dt\longrightarrow0.
\tag{50}
\]
For simple predictable controls stopped at guard exit, successive
conditional Gaussian integrations and (47) telescope.  Since
\(\mathcal L^u=\sum_ju_j\mathcal L^{e_j}\), every such control has scaled
risk at least
\[
\phi^-(0,0,0)-\int_0^1e_B(t)\,dt.
\tag{51}
\]
All quantities are bounded on the guard box, so stochastic-integral
approximation extends (51) to every progressively measurable control.
This validates the lower endpoint directly and does not invoke global
generalized-terminal comparison.

For the upper endpoint, the grid recursion selects a predictable
piecewise-constant policy, and the independent fixed-policy recursion,
again using (39), encloses its actual risk.  Predictable simple simplex
processes \(v^{(N)}\) approximate every admissible control \(u\) with
\[
\mathbb E\int_0^1\|u(t)-v^{(N)}(t)\|_1\,dt\longrightarrow0.
\tag{52}
\]
The Itô isometry and the square-root inequality give
\[
\mathbb E\|Q^u(1)-Q^{v^{(N)}}(1)\|_1\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
\sum_j\mathbb E\left|
\int_0^1(\sqrt{u_j(t)}-\sqrt{v_j^{(N)}(t)})\,dW_j(t)
\right|^2\longrightarrow0.
\tag{53}
\]
The scenario drift difference is at most \(H\) times the first quantity.
Equations (34) and (53) yield convergence of every regularized scenario
risk, uniformly over the finite scenario list.  Approximating the finitely
many simple action values by the rational control net using (44) completes
the upper approximation.  Combining it with (50)--(51) proves convergence
of the two regularized Bellman endpoints to the same continuous-control
value.  At a fixed partition, backward conditioning makes the current
score, clock, and likelihood vector a sufficient Markov state.  If
\(v_j=0\), (43) fixes coordinate \(j\) and (45) gives it zero coefficient;
no forced exploration is required.

\emph{Guard control.}
Under scenario \(m\),
\[
X_j(t)=h_j^mQ_j(t)+M_j(t),\qquad
M_j(t)=\int_0^t\sqrt{u_j(s)}\,dW_j(s),\qquad0\leq Q_j(t)\leq1.
\]
Successive Gaussian conditioning and simple-process approximation show
that \(\exp\{\theta M_j(t)-\theta^2Q_j(t)/2\}\) is a mean-one nonnegative
martingale.  Applying
\(\mathrm{lem{:}howard\mbox{-}linear\mbox{-}boundary}\) to both signs and
using \(|h_j^m|\leq H\) gives, uniformly over \(m\) and \(u\),
\[
\Pr_m^u\!\left\{\max_j\sup_{t\leq1}|X_j(t)|>G\right\}
\leq2K\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(G-H)^2}{2}\right\},\qquad G>H.
\tag{54}
\]
Thus exterior intervals affect risk only through the certified probability
in (54), which vanishes as \(G\to\infty\).

\emph{Minimax assembly and termination.}
Define
\[
\mathcal G(\lambda)=B(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_m
=\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_m\lambda_mr_m(u).
\tag{55}
\]
Because \(r_m(u)\in[0,1]\),
\[
|\mathcal G(\lambda)-\mathcal G(\lambda')|
\leq\|\lambda-\lambda'\|_1.
\tag{56}
\]
The rational simplex net with denominator \(D\) contains every point mass
and has \(\ell_1\)-radius at most \(2(M-1)/D\).
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}least\mbox{-}favorable\mbox{-}saddle}\) gives
\[
V=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\mathcal G(\lambda).
\tag{57}
\]
At every prior-net point, (33) gives
\[
B_\delta^-(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,\delta}^+
\leq\mathcal G(\lambda)\leq
B_\delta^+(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,\delta}^-.
\tag{58}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}quantitative\mbox{-}terminal\mbox{-}comparison}\), the
width in (58) is at most
\[
\bigl(B_\delta^+-B_\delta^-\bigr)
+\sum_m\lambda_m(c_{m,\delta}^+-c_{m,\delta}^-)
\leq2\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\eta),
\tag{59}
\]
and \(\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\sqrt\delta)\to0\).
Equations (56)--(59), together with the validated point-mass recursions,
give certified dual bounds including the oracle offsets.

For a finite policy mixture with weights \(p_s\), suppose the independent
fixed-policy recursion gives scenario-risk intervals
\([L_m^-,L_m^+]\) and the point-mass recursion gives oracle intervals
\([c_m^-,c_m^+]\).  Then
\[
V\leq\max_m\{L_m^+-c_m^-\}.
\tag{60}
\]
This upper endpoint is valid independently of the optimization recursion
that selected the mixture.

All lower endpoints converge upward to \(V\) by (39), (48), (50),
(54), and (56)--(59), as the prior radius, terminal width, guard-exit
probability, state and control meshes, Gaussian cells and tails, and
rounding errors vanish.  Every occurrence of scaled-datum continuity in
this list is charged using \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\).
For upper endpoints, take the finite \(\epsilon\)-saddle mixture of Markov
Bayes responses supplied by
\(\mathrm{thm{:}least\mbox{-}favorable\mbox{-}saddle}\).  A net prior
within radius \(r_\lambda\) of its least-favorable prior makes each
component \(2r_\lambda\)-Bayes, since both a fixed policy's Bayes risk and
the Bayes value are \(1\)-Lipschitz in the prior.  Equations (52)--(53)
approximate the finitely many components by enumerated grid policies, which
are eventually retained.  Their mixture is feasible for the rational
scenario-risk linear program, while (54), (59), and the independent
recursion make (60) at most \(V+\epsilon+o(1)\).  Letting
\(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves downward convergence of the cumulative
primal endpoints to \(V\).

Every candidate computation is finite.  Gaussian probabilities and
elementary functions admit terminating rational Taylor enclosures on
bounded cells, omitted tails use (54), and both optimization problems are
finite rational linear programs.  The deterministic enumeration contains
\(\delta\downarrow0\), \(\eta=\sqrt\delta\), \(G\uparrow\infty\), and
the nested refinements in (48).  Recomputing every affected ledger term
from (39) shows that the actual ledger sum tends to zero.  Thus, for every
\(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}>0\), some finite candidate has certified gap
at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), so the search reaches it and
terminates.  Cumulative maxima of lower endpoints and minima of
independently validated upper endpoints are monotone and valid.  At
termination,
\[
\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon},
\qquad
\overline V_{\varepsilon}-\underline V_{\varepsilon}
\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}},
\]
and the independently evaluated mixture satisfies
\(\max_mr_m(u)\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}\).

Finally,
\(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\).
Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}boundary\mbox{-}stable\mbox{-}frontier}\) transfers
the returned mixture's scenario-risk vector to predictable finite-horizon
policies and gives \(c_{n,m}\to c_m\).  Since \(M\) is finite,
\[
\max_mr_{n,m}(\pi_n)=\max_mr_m(u)+o(1)
\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}+o(1).
\]
Only the exact finite scenario list and \(|h_j^m|\leq H\) were used; no
null-boundary closure premise is needed.  The proof establishes termination
and certified convergence, but no closed-form mesh size, arithmetic
complexity bound, or convergence rate.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every finite \(\mathcal H_0\subset[-H,H]^K\), the fixed Gaussian grid experiment is exactly embedded by vertex controls in the score diffusion. For arbitrary predictable policies, including policies on zero-allocation faces, the discontinuous closed-test terminal loss satisfies
\[
\sup_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}|B_n(\lambda)-B(\lambda)|\longrightarrow0,
\qquad c_{n,m}\longrightarrow c_m\quad(1\leq m\leq M),
\qquad V_n\longrightarrow V.
\]
Moreover, for each \(\epsilon>0\) there are predictable finite-horizon policies whose scenario-risk vectors converge coordinatewise to that of an \(\epsilon\)-optimal diffusion control.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The mathematical conclusions are unchanged, but the unscoped strict-extension label is positioning rather than a theorem claim. The replacement states the exact embedding, boundary-stable convergence, and policy-transfer conclusions proved.

proposed.name: finite monotone primal-dual certificate algorithm
proposed.construction:
Given \(\mathfrak E\) and \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), enumerate deterministically all finite binary-rational candidates consisting of lower and upper terminal-envelope widths \(\delta\), small-information cutoffs \(\eta\), an inner score box and a strictly larger guard box, time and allocation-clock meshes, a finite rational control net in the allocation simplex, a finite rational prior net in \(\Delta_M\) containing every point mass, a rational near-Bayes retention tolerance, a partition of a truncated standardized Gaussian box into rational cells, and an outward-rounding precision.  Put \(c_H=H+H^2/2\).  For the normalized posterior terminal payoff use
\[
\Omega_\delta(d)=\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+2Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\]
For each prior \(\lambda\), let \(C_G\) be the computable maximum of \(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\) on the guard box, write \(S=(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m)/C_G\), and scale the lower and upper regularized versions of \(F_\lambda\) by \(C_G^{-1}\).  For the resulting scaled unnormalized datum \(Sg\), use throughout
\[
\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=
\min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+3Kc_H\right)d\right\}.
\]
Propagate the scaled values backward on the viable state cells and undo the scale at the initial state.  At a state cell of diameter \(d\), the interval interpolant is the barycentric sum of the vertex intervals enlarged by \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)\).  Use this same scaled-datum modulus in state and control-net estimates whenever terminal continuity is invoked, in mollification error, in Bellman residual and finite-horizon accumulation, in every fixed-policy and point-mass-oracle recursion, and in the corresponding entries of the actual certificate ledger; when its linear expression is at least one, use the range bound one.

For every control-net point, scenario, and retained Gaussian cell, outward-round the cell probability, enclose the entire image of that cell under the score-clock transition, multiply the probability interval by the resulting continuation interval, and sum outward.  Use the interval \([0,1]\) only for transitions outside the guard box and for omitted Gaussian-tail mass.  A rational compactly supported mollification of the multilinear interpolants is checked cell by cell against the reference-law Bellman operators; Taylor's formula with integral remainder supplies a certified time-discretization and control residual, and the same recursion supplies its finite-horizon accumulated bound.  Run the identical validated recursion at every point-mass prior to enclose the regularized versions of \(c_m\).  Retain every enumerated grid policy certified to be near-Bayes at some prior-net point, solve outward-rounded rational primal and dual scenario-risk linear programs over those columns, and independently re-evaluate the selected finite policy mixture by a fixed-policy interval recursion.  Extend the dual search from the prior net using the \(\ell_1\)-Lipschitz bound for the Bayes-regret functional.

Form a ledger from the actual certified terminal-regularization, guard-exit, time-discretization, scaled-datum interpolation and control-mesh, Gaussian-cell, Gaussian-tail, mollification and Bellman-residual accumulation, oracle and linear-program, recovered-policy, prior-net, and rounding contributions, with every scaled-datum continuity contribution recomputed from \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\).  Replace each lower endpoint by the maximum and each upper endpoint by the minimum over all candidates examined so far.  Accept the first candidate for which the sum of the applicable certified ledger bounds is at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\); call the resulting cumulative endpoints \(\underline V_{\varepsilon}\) and \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\).

prose_updates.tldr: For any declared finite bounded list of local causal-effect scenarios, the fixed arithmetic-mean closed e-test admits an adaptive subgroup-recruitment minimax-regret frontier. Exact Gaussian grid embedding and a quantitative terminal-envelope comparison transfer its discontinuous rejection risk, including zero-allocation faces, to and from the controlled score diffusion. Finite-scenario convex duality yields an attained least-favorable prior and posterior-state Markov response. A deterministic nested interval Bellman search supplies convergent certified bounds and an independently checked policy mixture. This object is complementary to the repository's unrestricted finite-population binary-contrast design-and-estimation frontier.

project_justification.gap: Regular-payoff adaptive-experiment diffusion results and the low-information posterior-control diffusion of Araman--Caldentey do not establish transfer for a fixed closed-testing multiple-decision rule with discontinuous terminal loss, nor a minimax policy-recovery certificate. The complementary repository record \(\mathtt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\) instead optimizes unrestricted design and estimation for fixed finite-population binary contrasts through an exact \(2^K\) response-type game and an \(n^{-4/3}\) second-order minimax-MSE bracket; it does not solve predictable subgroup recruitment for the fixed e-test and local-Gaussian missed-discovery regret studied here.
project_justification.niche: Holding the confirmatory closed e-test fixed isolates the design problem of predictably recruiting among prespecified subgroups under a finite list of local Gaussian causal-effect scenarios. The resulting target is a robust weighted missed-discovery regret frontier with legal zero-information faces.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact Gaussian grid embedding, quantitative boundary-stable transfer for the discontinuous rejection surfaces, uniform Bayes and oracle convergence, minimax-regret convergence, predictable finite-policy attainment, and an attained least-favorable-prior posterior-state reduction. It also proves termination of a deterministic nested interval-Bellman search whose corrected scaled-datum modulus and actual error ledger validate both the value interval and an independently re-evaluated policy mixture.

prose_updates.related_work: The accepted repository record \(\mathtt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\) is complementary, not a strict-extension predecessor: it optimizes unrestricted design and estimation for fixed finite-population binary contrasts, using an exact \(2^K\) response-type game and an \(n^{-4/3}\) second-order minimax-MSE bracket with certificates. This note instead fixes the arithmetic-mean closed e-test and optimizes predictable subgroup recruitment under finite local-Gaussian scenarios for weighted missed-discovery regret, proving an initial-state diffusion frontier across discontinuous rejection surfaces and a validated interval-Bellman policy certificate. Wager and Xu supply a weak-signal score-clock diffusion donor; Adusumilli's risk-policy and allocation-process work supplies regular-payoff control and finite-to-continuous architecture. Araman--Caldentey supplies a low-information posterior-control diffusion for a regular terminal action or reward, but not closed-testing multiple-decision discontinuous-payoff transfer or a minimax policy-recovery certificate. Burnett--Jennison and Ballarini et al. study prior-weighted enrichment under frequentist error control. Rosenblum--Fang--Liu and Baas--ter Schure--van Rosmalen motivate, respectively, sparse finite-stage enrichment optimization and scalar e-value dynamic programming, but neither supplies the present two-sided validated continuum certificate with an independent recovered-policy check.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The common-drift translation and initial-state envelope squeeze do not prove comparison or uniqueness at every off-origin viable boundary state. The certificate therefore uses direct finite-horizon Bellman enclosure and stopped-process verification for continuous terminal envelopes, not global generalized-terminal HJB uniqueness. Its scaled unnormalized reference datum requires the corrected modulus \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=\min\{1,(32/\delta+3K(H+H^2/2))d\}\), and every affected ledger term is recomputed from that modulus. Termination is qualitative and computable; no closed-form mesh schedule, arithmetic operation count, convergence rate, or interval-certified nontrivial numerical run is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The frontier and saddle results assume known unit Gaussian variance, finitely many prespecified disjoint subgroups, positive normalized missed-discovery weights, fixed elementary e-alternatives, the arithmetic-mean closure rule, and an arbitrary finite scenario set in \([-H,H]^K\). No positive lower bound on subgroup allocation is imposed. Null-boundary closure is optional application structure, not a theorem or certificate premise. The note fixes the test and optimizes recruitment; it does not compete with unrestricted joint design-and-estimation minimax theory. Unknown variance, delayed responses, overlapping or data-discovered subgroups, and optimization of the confirmatory test are outside scope. Global generalized-terminal comparison and uniqueness at viable off-origin boundary states remain open.

statement_notes.justification: It identifies the attainable local-power regret frontier for the fixed confirmatory test on every finite bounded scenario list and transfers a near-optimal diffusion risk vector to predictable finite-stage recruitment.
statement_notes.gap: The theorem is not positioned as an unqualified strict extension. Wager--Xu and Adusumilli supply regular-payoff diffusion architecture, while Araman--Caldentey supplies a low-information posterior-control donor; none supplies the boundary-stable discontinuous closed-test transfer proved here. The repository's multi-arm second-order minimax frontier is complementary because it concerns unrestricted finite-population binary-contrast design and estimation rather than fixed-test local-Gaussian subgroup recruitment.
statement_notes.consumer: It converts a continuum recruitment solution into asymptotically equivalent finite-stage policies for interAdapt-style subgroup-enrichment designs.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives a reproducible epsilon certificate because every scaled-datum continuity contribution is computed from the corrected modulus, every accepted endpoint is backed by a candidate-specific rational ledger, and the returned policy mixture is independently re-evaluated.
